merger_description:
Pursuant to the Term Sheet between:

* MEC Oceania Investment Pty Ltd (**MEA**);
* Eynesbury AK1 Pty Ltd atf Eynesbury AK1 Trust, and Eynesbury AK2 Pty Ltd atf Eynesbury AK2 Trust (**RMax**); and
* Resimax Group Proprietary Limited

MEA intends that its wholly-owned subsidiary MECO Eynesbury Pty Limited (MECO) acquires 49.9% of the equity interests, via a subscription for preference shares, in each of Eynesbury Greenhill Pty Ltd, Eynesbury Wyndham Pty Ltd, and Eynesbury Township Pty Ltd (the **Eynesbury Entities**) (the **Acquisition**).

Following the Acquisition, RMax will hold the remaining 50.1% equity stake in the Eynesbury Entities.

The Eynesbury Entities (including via current subsidiary Eynesbury Quarter Hospitality Trading Pty Ltd and future subsidiary Eynesbury Water Pty Ltd) own land and commercial businesses in connection with the development of a residential master planned community development project in Eynesbury, Victoria (the **Eynesbury MPC**). The Eynesbury MPC is under development, and the Acquisition is to provide further capital to fund the development.

The Eynesbury Entities are wholly owned subsidiaries of RMax.

MECO is a special purpose acquisition vehicle and wholly owned subsidiary of MEA, the Australian investment vehicle of Japan based real-estate investment group, Mitsubishi Estate.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between MECO or MEA and
the Eynesbury Entities in the supply of residential MPC
housing in Eynesbury and the surrounding areas, nor in the
Western Melbourne Corridor more broadly
b. there are several alternative suppliers of residential MPC
housing to customers in the Western Melbourne Corridor.
The ACCC has also had regard to the likelihood that, if the
Acquisition were put into effect, the notification thresholds
determined under section 51ABP(1) of the Act would apply.
While the ACCC considers that the notification thresholds are likely
to be met, given that material competition concerns are unlikely to
arise, the ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required
to be notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
